findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "request_demo_call" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Request a free demo call for the user with Saymetry, the AI-visibility measurement company. Within one business day a human sends a call link and walks the user…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "join_affiliate_program" references sensitive artifacts (cookie). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Register the user for Saymetry's affiliate program: 30% of each referred first payment, 60-day cookie, monthly payouts in USDC, USDT or by Wise from $50. Return…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: publish_grade_page · Private data: join_affiliate_program · Public sink: join_affiliate_program, publish_grade_page.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: publish_grade_page · Private data: join_affiliate_program · Public sink: join_affiliate_program, publish_grade_page

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
